solves.reason: (A) 'lead naturally to ___ data' + later 'yield quantitative data' confirms quantitative. (B) memory study 'items an individual can ___' = recall. (C) 'seek concrete responses' confirms concrete.
(A) 'also ___ quantitative data' = yield (produce). (B) 'might not be ___' followed by issues = reliable. (C) '___ consistency from one study to the next' = ensure.

(A) 'recollections may be ___' = inaccurate (problems with memory). (B) 'definitions could ___ widely' = vary. (C) 'make ___ concepts clearer' = abstract (the point is making abstract things concrete).
①measure ②recall ③reliable all match original. ④shows 'accurate' but original says 'inaccurate' — contradiction.
①quantitative ②yield ④concrete match original. ③shows 'converge' but original says 'vary widely' — opposite meaning.
②procrastinator ③afford ④consistency match original. ①shows 'ambiguous' but original says 'concrete' — opposite.
'A study might ___ the number of times' = measure. Only measure fits the research context.
'might not be ___' = reliable. The passage argues some data lacks reliability.
'ensure ___ from one study to the next' = consistency. Research needs consistency.
yield = produce (both mean to generate/create output). Other options don't match.
ensure = guarantee (both mean to make certain). suggest/measure/recall are different.
vary = differ (both mean to be different). remain is opposite, others unrelated.
reliable antonym: questionable (doubtful/unreliable). consistent & accurate are synonyms, concrete is different axis.
abstract antonym: concrete (tangible/specific). vague & theoretical are similar to abstract, general is different axis.
(A) 'measure the number' = 측정하다. (B) 'a new measure to reduce pollution' = 조치/방안. Answer: 측정하다-조치 = ④.
'habitually delays or postpones tasks' = procrastinator. Clear definition match.
Possessive 'Respondents'' requires noun. recollect → recollections (plural noun for memories).
'ensure ___' needs noun object. consistent (adj) → consistency (noun).
Context: asking specific question '___' — prompts a concrete answer fits the before/after logic perfectly.
'help make ___' = abstract concepts clearer. The whole passage argues concrete questions clarify abstract concepts.
